question: A collection \(S\) of points \((x,y)\) of the plane is said to be convex if whenever two points \(P=(u,v)\) and \(Q=(s,t)\) belong to \(S\), every point on the line segment \(PQ\) also belongs to \(S\). Let \(S_1\) be the collection of all points \((x,y)\) for which \(1<x^2+y^2<2\) and let \(S_2\) be the collection of all points \((x,y)\) for which \(x\) and \(y\) have the same sign. Then

options.A: \(S_1\) is convex and \(S_2\) is not convex;
options.D: \(S_1\) is not convex and \(S_2\) is convex.

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10+2 Level — Sixteenth Edition
